newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia banks launch electronic bill pay service.
newsitem.headline: Australia banks launch electronic bill pay service.

text.p: Ten Australian banks on Tuesday launched an automated bill payment service called BPAY which will allow consumers to pay bills electronically through participating institutions.
The scheme, which will be open to all deposit taking institutions, is expected to be available to consumers by the last quarter of 1997.
The ten banks are Advance Bank, ANZ Bank, Bank SA, BankWest, Challenge Bank, Colonial State Bank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, National Australia Bank, St George and Westpac Banking Corp.

"This new service will enable consumers to pay their bills with just one contact with their participating bank, building society or credit union," Linda Hemstrom, BPAY's national business manager said in a statement.

Each financial institution in the scheme will compete to offer their customers electronic payment alternatives which are initially based on telephone banking and in some cases will include personal computer and internet options.

Hemstrom said the benefit for customers would be in paying their bills in the knowledge their personal banking details were secure while businesses would benefit by receiving cleared funds usually on the same day.

Hemstrom told Reuters the scheme had already received a favourable response from a number of government authorities and consumer groups including the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA), the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) and the Australian Consumer Association (ACA).
